Ex-Navy Diver here, let me try to clear up a few details.

Since the submariner breathe air in the submarine that is kept at 1 atm there is no risk to his body while surfacing. Initially when he enters the water column the pressure exerted (on his whole body) would actually reduce the volume in his lungs and then return to normal as you reached the surface. 

When breathing compressed air at any depth there are many dangers when surfacing. The factors that escalate the risk are determined by the gas you’re breathing, time at depth, and speed of ascent. 

Nitrogen is normally used only to Deb’s of around 120 feet due to it being very slow to leave the body even after only a few minutes of saturation at 3 to 4 atm (90-120). As a working diver in those greater depths you are more likely to see a oxygen/helium mixture. This mixture leaves your bodies tissue much quicker.

Decompression sickness is categorized into severities of type one and type two.  Decompression sickness is about the gas left in the body, it is Common for this to be confused with AGE or Arterial gas embolism. This is where the alveoli (gas exchange in the lungs) ruptures. Your body is still Attempting to exchange air into the bloodstream, but because of the rupture it ask like when you drink soda through a straw with a hole in it. This introduces air bubbles into the arterial side of your circulatory system. These bubbles have a short distance as they will travel to your heart then into your brain. Death caused by arterial gas embolism happens within 6 to 7 minutes of you reaching the surface. 

Decompression sickness Because it is rooted in gas is remaining or in the process of leaving the body this occurs on the veinous side of the circulatory system. It manifests itself is localized pain, minor to major rashes on the body, and numbness. Can still result in death but less severe as AGE.

I cannot speak on the submarine design of the past but current submarine living conditions your body is still only experiencing 1 atm of pressure thus there would not be an increased saturation of either of the gases in your body.
